content: Cordlife Ltd is a company specializing in cord blood banking, headquartered in Singapore and publicly traded on the Australian Stock Exchange. The organization operates three cord blood processing and storage facilities located in Singapore, Hong Kong, Jakarta (Indonesia), and Sydney (Australia). The company was established in May 2001, making it one of the earliest private cord blood banks in Southeast Asia and the first of its kind in Singapore. In December 2002, Cordlife facilitated the first cord blood transplant in Singapore using a privately banked cord blood unit. In April 2003, Cordlife acquired Cytomatrix LLC, a company based in Massachusetts, USA. Subsequently, in June 2004, the company underwent a corporate restructuring and rebranded itself as CyGenics Ltd (ASX:CYN), listing on the Australian Stock Exchange. Following this, the company expanded its operations into Southeast Asia and North Asia, inaugurating a facility in Hong Kong in March 2005. In September 2005, the Singapore facility achieved accreditation from the American Association of Blood Banks (AABB), making it the only private cord blood bank in the region to hold this distinction. In November 2005, the company entered the Australian market by acquiring a majority stake in BioCell Pty Ltd. In January 2006, Cordlife established a presence in Kolkata, India, with the event attended by Singapore’s Senior Minister Goh Chok Tong. By September 2006, the company announced plans to open a facility in Jakarta, Indonesia. This facility officially commenced operations in September 2007, while the Kolkata facility was projected to open by the end of 2007. Additionally, the company expressed intentions to establish a larger facility in Singapore. In December 2006, Cordlife was recognized as a Technology Pioneer for 2007 by the World Economic Forum. Finally, in March 2007, the company rebranded itself as Cordlife Ltd to emphasize its core focus on cord blood banking services.
